entries.mem0ai/mem0: Mem0 is a universal memory layer for AI agents and an official Hermes Agent memory provider, available as managed cloud or Apache-2.0 self-hosted open source. It supports semantic, keyword, and entity-based retrieval, with SDKs, a CLI, and a self-hosted server.
entries.vectorize-io/hindsight: Hindsight provides long-term agent memory through retain, recall, and reflect operations. It supports hosted and local LLM providers and offers Docker, pip, and Kubernetes deployment options.
entries.volcengine/OpenViking: OpenViking is an open-source context database and official Hermes Agent memory provider that organizes agent context as browsable files and directories. Its scoped retrieval uses L0, L1, and L2 loading tiers; the project reports 91% token reduction and a 43–49% task-completion gain over baseline on LoCoMo10.
entries.topoteretes/cognee: Cognee is an open-source memory platform that structures text as entities, relationships, and searchable chunks for agents. It supports custom data models and ontologies, plus plugins and MCP for connecting agents.
entries.supermemoryai/supermemory: Supermemory is a memory engine and API, as well as an official Hermes Agent memory provider, that extracts conversation facts and handles contradictions and automatic forgetting. It connects to services including Google Drive, Gmail, Notion, OneDrive, and GitHub, and processes PDFs, images, videos, and code.
entries.garrytan/gbrain: Gbrain is an opinionated brain for OpenClaw and Hermes Agent that stores facts with provenance and supports corrections and withdrawal. It can share memory across agents while keeping transient task state local, with optional semantic search, synthesis, and background enrichment.
entries.plastic-labs/honcho: Honcho is a memory library for building stateful agents, tracking peers, sessions, and messages over time. It supports managed, local, and self-hosted deployments and provides Python and TypeScript SDKs; the elkimek/honcho-self-hosted Hermes wrapper builds on it.
entries.campfirein/byterover-cli: ByteRover CLI treats memory as a Git repo, managing a context tree with Git-like version control. It is an official Hermes Agent memory provider with five retrieval tiers, four of them non-LLM and sub-100ms, plus a React/Ink TUI and REPL.
entries.mnemosyne-oss/mnemosyne: Mnemosyne is a SQLite-backed memory layer for Hermes agents, described as zero-dependency and sub-millisecond, with one pure-Python dependency. It integrates through MCP, native providers, or a Python SDK; its BEAM results are reported for v3.0.0, while LongMemEval is pending.
entries.moorcheh-ai/memanto: Memanto extracts knowledge from agent interaction streams, then consolidates, reconciles, and forgets memories. It can export memory in Open Knowledge Format.
entries.ClaudioDrews/memory-os: Memory OS is a seven-layer memory system for Hermes Agent that includes vector search, structured facts, fabric recall, and an auto-curated wiki. It uses local infrastructure with Docker, Qdrant, Redis, and SQLite, and a Ground Truth hierarchy to prioritize injected context.
entries.greyhaven-ai/autocontext: Autocontext is a recursive self-improving context harness that helps agents tackle complex tasks by running tasks against evaluation. It keeps useful lessons, discards dead ends, and leaves traces, reports, and playbooks.
entries.stephenschoettler/hermes-lcm: This Hermes Agent plugin uses a SQLite store and hierarchical DAG to persist messages, with the stated goal of never losing a message. Its lcm_grep and lcm_recall tools help recover details from stored context.
entries.vshulcz/deja-vu: Deja-vu searches session histories across supported coding agents, making past conversations available during current work. It can also sync history between machines over SSH.
entries.elkimek/honcho-self-hosted: This project provides a self-hosted Honcho backend for private, cross-session memory in Hermes Agent. It supports OpenAI-compatible providers and local inference servers, with an automated setup script for Docker, PostgreSQL, and Redis.
entries.Signet-AI/signetai: Signet provides a local-first identity, memory, and secrets layer with portable state across Hermes Agent and other supported clients. It can import files, webpages, and agent conversations, and includes a dashboard for browsing memories and sources.
entries.plur-ai/plur: Plur stores shared agent memory as plain-text YAML engrams on disk, with local search available after a one-time model download and keyword fallback. Its README reports 95.6% R@5 on LongMemEval-S (N=500).
entries.yoloshii/ClawMem: ClawMem is an on-device memory and context engine that combines BM25 and vector search with rank fusion and cross-encoder reranking. It can generate session handoffs and capture decisions and preferences, with integrations through hooks, MCP, and native agent plugins.
entries.Sibyl-Labs/Sibyl-Memory: Sibyl-Memory keeps long-term memory in a local SQLite file and provides FTS5 search with a five-tier schema. Its package family includes an SDK, CLI, Hermes adapter, MCP server, and LangGraph BaseStore, without requiring a vector database or embeddings.
entries.EfficientContext/ContextPilot: ContextPilot optimizes context ordering for prefix-cache sharing, including text and multimodal contexts. It provides a context index for reordering, deduplication, and cache-aware scheduling, and integrates with Hermes Agent as well as other listed runtimes.
entries.yantrikos/yantrikdb-hermes-plugin: This Hermes memory plugin uses an embedded backend by default, with an HTTP backend also available. Recall results include a why_retrieved reason, and the plugin supports contradiction tracking and memory canonicalization.
entries.JanYork/llm-wiki-cli: This agent-driven CLI maintains a persistent, source-grounded Wiki with citations and history across sessions. It is designed to recall, maintain, and evolve knowledge without embeddings or a vector database.
entries.ccf/agentcairn: AgentCairn stores durable memory as inspectable Markdown files with frontmatter, using an Obsidian vault as the source of truth. A local DuckDB cache supports hybrid search and retrieval, while MCP servers and host-specific plugins connect it to coding agents.
entries.amanning3390/flowstate-qmd: Flowstate-QMD watches agent session logs to prefetch context into an anticipatory cache. It uses local SQLite-vec storage and GGUF models via node-llama-cpp, and provides an MCP-native server with automated configuration for major coding-agent clients.
entries.yepyhun/Brainstack: Brainstack combines Hindsight, Graphiti, and MemPalace under a single memory owner, using SQLite, Kuzu, and Chroma for state and retrieval management. It gives Hermes a purpose-built evidence packet for each query.
entries.generalbusiness-ai/keep: Keep indexes codebases, URLs, and multimedia, including through OCR, and supports semantic search with BM25 full-text search and ranked graph traversal. Its edge tags link notes in navigable, bidirectional relationships.
entries.aliasocracy/hermes-tool-slimmer: Hermes Tool Slimmer reduces tool-schema tokens with local keyword-based ranking and Tool Search support. It integrates as middleware without patching Hermes core on version 0.19 and later, and includes a dashboard for savings and tool configurations.
entries.conorbronsdon/agent-context-os: Agent Context OS is a Git-backed context and workflow layer for Claude Code, Codex, and other supported coding agents. It includes workflows for migration, handoffs, and memory proposals; integrations are opt-in rather than enabled automatically.
entries.Ladybug-Memory/hermes-memory-plugin: This local-only Hermes memory plugin stores data in a single .lbdb embedded graph database file and supports BM25 keyword search with named graph relationships. Its importance-weighted recall brings higher-priority memories forward during context prefetch.
entries.stepanov1975/hermes-local-knowledge: Hermes Local Knowledge indexes configured local sources and selected Hermes runtime sources for capability search and routing. It registers five tools for search, retrieval, traversal, feedback, and usage reports, along with three lifecycle hooks.
entries.MukundaKatta/hermes-agentmemory: This pull-model episodic memory plugin supports immediate event deletion, without persistent summaries that could affect later recall. It uses an on-demand summarizer and records prefetch operations in a trace.jsonl audit log.
entries.hermes-labs-ai/hermes-blind: Hermes Blind recovers the original goal from the first user turn of a long Claude Code or Codex session, with goals, first-sentence, and full extraction modes. It skips tool output and other non-user-turn records, and does not use a summarizing model or external service.
entries.piprail/piprail: Piprail provides a TypeScript SDK for x402 payments and an MCP server for budget-bound agent wallets. It operates without a backend, database, or API keys.
entries.yonro/hermes-xmemo-plugin: This Hermes memory provider runs inside Hermes and communicates with XMemo over HTTPS for durable cross-session memory with semantic search. It supplies ranked, bounded context recall before a turn and includes a local SQLite reliability layer.
entries.futurebrowser/hermes-exabase-plugin: The Exabase memory plugin integrates Exabase M-1 for self-organizing long-term agent memory. It offers tools for searching and manually storing memories, plus configurable query expansion and result reranking.
entries.sourcevault-ai/sourcevault-code-tools: SourceVault Code Tools provides private local code memory for repositories, with semantic search, file reads, and grounded Q&A. Its slash commands cover search, file reads, context, and Q&A, while repo sync and indexed git-history search support work across Hermes CLI, Telegram, and Hermes Desktop.
entries.visorcraft/MongrelDB-Hermes: MongrelDB-Hermes provides long-term memory for Hermes Agent, with AES-256-GCM encryption at rest enabled by default. It offers HNSW approximate-nearest-neighbor, sparse, and FM-index retrieval, and can run through native Rust FFI or an HTTP daemon.
entries.penfieldlabs/hermes-penfield: Penfield provides memory tools for Hermes Agent, including 17 tools for memory management and knowledge-graph traversal. Its hybrid search combines BM25, vector, and graph methods, and it can automatically checkpoint context during message compression.
entries.conorbronsdon/agent-memory-kit: Agent Memory Kit curates agent memory stored in plain Markdown files, proposing evidence-cited JSON diffs for review rather than using a database. Its “rot” and “lint” curators find stale or conflicting facts, while a local Git repository tracks and can revert changes.

entries.obra/superpowers: Superpowers is an agentic skills framework and software development methodology built around composable skills that instruct agents to use them. Its workflow spans specification, design sign-off, planning, and subagent execution, with separate installation instructions for multiple harnesses.
entries.nexu-io/open-design: Open Design is a local-first system for creating and refining interactive web prototypes with a live preview, as well as slide decks, images, and motion graphics. It includes skills, design templates, design systems, and plugins, and supports coding-agent CLIs including Hermes Agent.
entries.mukul975/Anthropic-Cybersecurity-Skills: This project provides structured cybersecurity skills spanning 34 security domains. Its highlights describe mappings to MITRE ATT&CK, ATLAS, D3FEND, and F3, and compatibility with more than 26 AI platforms.
entries.Agents365-ai/drawio-skill: Drawio-skill turns natural-language descriptions into editable .drawio diagrams, using prompts and real sources. Its incremental sync preserves manual layout and annotations, and it offers the diagramctl CLI with an optional MCP server.
entries.internet-court/internet-court-skill: Internet Court provides a master router and connector skills for agent-to-agent commerce. It includes vendored copies of official protocol skills and adds a verification and dispute-resolution layer.
entries.conorbronsdon/avoid-ai-writing: Avoid AI Writing audits content and can rewrite it to address detectable AI writing patterns, with up to two editing passes. Its detector scores files or piped text, while in-place editing refuses source code, configuration, and generated data.
entries.AMAP-ML/SkillClaw: SkillClaw uses background evolution to automate skill deduplication and quality improvement. It also unifies skill libraries across agents, devices, and team members, and integrates with Hermes, Claude Code, Codex, and OpenAI-compatible APIs.
entries.wondelai/skills: This cross-platform skills library includes 51 expert frameworks and 14 guided metaskills. It supports Claude Code, Codex, and agent-plugins.org specifications, and maintains session state in the project's docs folder.
entries.mohitagw15856/pm-claude-skills: This project offers professional agent skills that run natively in Hermes Agent and Claude Code, with exports ready to paste into other assistants. Each skill includes a framework, output template, and quality checks; the README describes 1,295 skills and the project is MIT-licensed.
entries.ZeroPointRepo/youtube-skills: YouTube skills for Hermes Agent and other supported tools cover transcripts, video search, channel browsing, and playlist extraction. The listed compatible tools include OpenClaw, Claude Code, and Cursor; use requires a TranscriptAPI key, which has a 100-credit free tier.
entries.Romanescu11/hermes-skill-factory: Hermes Skill Factory watches active workflows to detect and propose reusable skills. It generates both SKILL.md documentation and Python plugin scaffolds, with slash commands to manage, list, and save detected patterns.
entries.Cranot/super-hermes: Super-Hermes helps Hermes Agent generate custom thinking instructions for specific tasks and includes pre-built analytical lenses for various domains. It reports findings alongside a report of analysis blind spots.
entries.DougTrajano/pydantic-ai-skills: Adds type-safe agentskills.io support for Pydantic AI, including remote skill registries sourced from Git and S3. It also provides tools for bundled resources and script execution, with sandboxing to isolate untrusted scripts from the host.
entries.tlehman/litprog-skill: Weaves prose, diagrams, and code into .lit.md documents, then extracts runnable source files from that documentation. Edits to extracted source files can also be synced back into the literate document, linking documentation and implementation.
entries.AkoliteZA/hermes-agent-idea-workflow: Turns rough ideas into structured design documents and implementation handoffs for Hermes Agent. Lite and Full modes accommodate different project complexity, while a spec review gate evaluates proposals with PASS/FAIL models.
entries.ReinaMacCredy/maestro: Provides a harness for long-running AI agents with structured memory, cross-feature learning, and a plan-approve-execute approach. It requires no background service and includes an SLP protocol for supervised teams, plus CLI commands for installation, updates, and diagnostics.
entries.esaradev/icarus-plugin: Shares agent memory across instances through Markdown files and automatically captures high-value decisions and outcomes. Its pipeline also supports fine-tuning and switching to replacement models.
entries.Hermes-brasil/hermes-brasil: Offers Portuguese-language Hermes Agent skills in SKILL.md format, alongside guides on installation, production, cron, MCP, and skill authoring. Contributions are submitted through pull requests, making the project a Portuguese-language resource for the community.
entries.black-forest-labs/skills: Provides prompting guidance for FLUX image and video generation, along with BFL API integration for polling and webhooks. Its FLUX 3 video suite includes eight specialist skills.
entries.smartcontractkit/chainlink-agent-skills: Lists nine Chainlink skills that follow the Agent Skills specification, with installation available through `npx skills add smartcontractkit/chainlink-agent-skills`. The README describes the repository as containing community examples only.
entries.armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge: Creates agent instructions from repositories, documentation, and developer discourse, with both automated and step-by-step workflows. It also includes skill testing and export.
entries.supernovae-st/nika: Nika checks workflows before calling a model, runs with a model of your choice, and verifies a tamper-evident record for each run. These features make it a workflow-focused option for this list.
entries.chigwell/skilldock.io: Provides a registry of reusable AI skills based on the AgentSkills specification, with both a Python SkilldockClient and a CLI. Skill installation supports recursive dependency resolution, and the project includes commerce features using TON payments.
entries.tiann/execplan-skill: Supports autonomous execution of long-running, multi-step tasks with real-time tracking of progress and decisions. Built-in rollback procedures provide a recovery path when execution needs to be reversed.
entries.adnw-vinc/hermes-nextcloud: Manage Nextcloud files, notes, calendars, tasks, and contacts through WebDAV and CalDAV. It uses HTTPS with Nextcloud App Passwords and includes a guided script to validate credentials and configure access.
entries.amanning3390/hermeshub: Browse, search, and install community skills through a hub that implements the Agentic Resource Discovery (ARD) v0.9 specification. It also offers federated search across GitHub and Hugging Face and operates via Hermes Agent on NVIDIA infrastructure.
entries.willingning-coder/eagle-eye: Retrieve relevant Hermes Agent skills through five layers, from hard triggers to semantic embeddings. By narrowing skill lists before LLM calls, it aims to reduce token usage, and it can degrade gracefully when embedding models or dependencies are unavailable.
entries.EntangledQuantum/Life_OS: Life_OS is an ADHD-friendly personal execution system with habits, study blocks, and agent control through MCP. It stores data in a single local SQLite file and includes a React web app and an Expo-based Android app.
entries.Sahil-SS9/hermaguard: Hermaguard performs read-only adversarial code reviews using parallel subagents for edge cases, adversarial review, and integration analysis. It combines a deterministic pre-scan with proof-of-concept execution in a hardened sandbox to verify findings.
entries.Sahil-SS9/hermes-simplify-swarm: This skill simplifies code using parallel Hygiene, Clarity, and Correctness agents, with a tiered application process and approval gate. It supports TypeScript, JavaScript, Python, Go, and Rust.
entries.handnewb/hermes-cybersec-lab: This cybersecurity lab brings together 2,077 skills from multiple repositories and installs 131+ tools for network work, forensics, and exploitation. It also integrates 28 cybersecurity frameworks and standards, including MITRE ATT&CK, MISP, and OWASP.
entries.teixeirazeus/fablize-for-hermes: Fablize for Hermes applies multi-story task decomposition with mandatory evidence-based verification gates. It also provides an investigation protocol for reproduction and causal debugging, plus a Python goal engine for persistent task state.
entries.PederHP/skillsdotnet: This C#/.NET implementation of agentskills.io uses SKILL.md files for progressive disclosure and integrates with Microsoft.Extensions.AI for tool-based skill loading. It can automatically register common agent skill directories.
entries.Diabloluo/hermes-hud: Hermes HUD is a local, real-time dashboard for tracking token costs, session history, and skill analytics. It keeps data access read-only and supports local log desensitization, with optional incident alerts via Telegram and Feishu.
entries.conorbronsdon/agent-skills: This collection provides production-tested skills for code review and session management, including multi-session reconciliation and worktree recovery. Skills are plain Markdown files that can be installed by copying a directory or using the bundled installer.
entries.conorbronsdon/demo-gif-skill: Creates reproducible VHS tape or Playwright recording scripts to add demo GIFs to project READMEs, supporting terminal CLIs, TUIs, web apps, and libraries. It also optimizes GIFs toward a target size under 8 MB, making it useful for documenting projects with compact, repeatable demos.
entries.conorbronsdon/agent-skill-builder: Generates Claude Code extensions and portable Agent Skills core files, then validates them against runtime-specific profiles with CI-friendly exit codes. It also monitors official frontmatter specifications weekly for field drift, helping keep skills aligned with current specs.
entries.aidevelopers2/remoteopenclaw-mcp: Searches a catalog of more than 13,870 MCP servers and 4,384 agent skills from a terminal or AI agent, and provides direct installation commands for discovered tools and plugins. Its MCP server integrates with clients including Hermes, Cursor, and Claude Code.
entries.Carlo1911/skill-evolution: Analyzes past sessions and installed skills to draft structured improvement proposals for AI agent skills. Proposals are review-only by default, with an evaluation gate that supports deterministic, LLM-judge, and regression evaluators.
entries.CorsenAI/hermes-windows-runtime-skills: Provides Hermes Agent skills for routing file operations with environment-specific path syntax and selecting and verifying existing, project-compatible Python interpreters. It supports native Windows, Git Bash/MSYS, and WSL environments.
entries.superagnt/leverage: Offers agent skills for social data, web research, and enrichment, along with packaged skills that combine an agent, skills, and a data flow. It also welcomes community skills in `skills/community/`.
entries.jiawood2006/hermes-skills: Provides tools for transcribing Douyin videos into structured Markdown and SRT subtitles, removing common Chinese AI-writing patterns with a rule-based engine, and extracting structured data from PDFs and images using macOS Vision. Its range of text, video, and document tasks makes it a multi-purpose collection of Hermes skills.
entries.webmilmind1/hermes-bounty-board: Lets agents list open support bounties, buy ticket context, and submit answers for human review; public wallet earnings records are also available. Users can create a bounty board and receive a URL, API key, and USDC deposit addresses.
entries.mag3nt-com/openclaw-skill: Automates USDC payments for HTTP 402 responses and supports Pay Link, x402, MPP, and AP2 protocols. It is compatible with OpenClaw, Hermes Agent, and the agentskills.io standard.
entries.skillseal/skillseal: Tests agent skills in isolated Docker containers for structure, functionality, and security, then issues certificates with Ed25519 signatures. It also provides a public API for certificate verification and skill submission.
entries.scavio-ai/hermes-agent: Connects Hermes Agent to structured web data across 31 platforms through a hosted MCP server that exposes 191 tools. The project also includes five workflow skills and supports Claude, Cursor, Goose, and OpenHands.
entries.parkyucheol-del/alphapipeline: Provides market data including DEX slippage and funding rates, and checks tokens for honeypot, tax, and liquidity risk. It makes these capabilities available through REST endpoints and a remote MCP server.
entries.Shine8592/china-briefing: This skill generates structured Chinese news briefings at multiple geographic scales, from global to street level. It adds user interests through semantic memory to expand searches, and includes core conclusions and action suggestions in its reports.
entries.aidatatools-dev/astro-agents-mcp: This project provides an MCP endpoint for Western and Vedic astrology with deterministic results and SHA-256 verifiable hashes. The endpoint requires no authentication and supports per-call REST payment via x402 or MPP.
entries.cablate/Agentic-MCP-Skill: Agentic-MCP-Skill is a progressive MCP client that uses three-layer loading to minimize token usage, with incremental discovery of server metadata and tool schemas. Its socket-based daemon architecture supports persistent connections, making it a distinctive option for Hermes agents that need to work with MCP servers.

entries.numtide/llm-agents.nix: This project packages AI coding agents and development tools with Nix, including Hermes, and provides a `nix run` command for listed tools. Its packages are updated automatically each day, making it a Nix-based option for running Hermes.
entries.marshallrichards/ClawPhone: ClawPhone collects scripts and notes for running agent CLIs, including Hermes Agent, on Android through Termux. Its highlights include an automated installer for Antigravity CLI on ARM64 Android, OpenClaw configuration guides, and hardware and UI access through Termux:API and Termux:GUI.
entries.AbuZar-Ansarii/Hermes-Agent-On-Android: This Termux-based installer and guide runs Hermes Agent on Android using proot-distro Ubuntu. It supports interactive model setup, gateway services, shell command execution, and external providers or local models via Ollama.
entries.ultraworkers/hermes-agent-helm-chart: This unofficial community Helm chart offers direct or operator-ready CRD-based workflows for deploying Hermes Agent on Kubernetes. It includes single-writer state-safety guardrails for persistent HERMES_HOME storage and configurable gateway mode with optional API and webhook listeners.
entries.amirghm/hermes-agent-mobile: This one-command installer brings the Hermes AI assistant to Android through Termux and to iOS through iSH. It also integrates with Telegram for voice and file messaging, and supports scheduled tasks via cron jobs on Termux.
entries.TheAiSingularity/hermesclaw: hermesclaw runs Hermes Agent with hardware-enforced sandboxing via NVIDIA OpenShell. It restricts network and filesystem access at the kernel level and offers configurable security policies for messaging and web search.
entries.solomon2773/nora: Nora is a self-hosted control plane for deploying, monitoring, and operating OpenClaw and Hermes agents on Docker or Kubernetes. It provides searchable logs, metrics, alert rules, and access through a REST API, CLI, and MCP server.
entries.xmbshwll/hermes-agent-docker: This project provides a Docker sandbox image for Hermes Agent that includes mini-swe-agent and the official Hermes installation. It supports persistent state through mounted home directories and lets users build specific Hermes tags with build arguments.
entries.0xrsydn/nix-hermes-agent: This project provides a Nix package and NixOS module for reproducible Hermes deployment, with declarative configuration for cli-config.yaml and workspace documents. It supports both Nix-managed and CLI-installed skills, and integrates secrets through systemd EnvironmentFiles and sops-nix.
entries.jpalmae/hermeshq: HermesHQ is a Docker-first control plane for running multiple Hermes Agent instances from one web application, with separate workspaces and identities. It provides per-agent Telegram and WhatsApp channels and granular policies for tools, paths, and network access.
entries.MilkyWay008/Hermes-OTG: Hermes OTG is a portable package that runs from a USB drive or other drive without host installation or registry writes. It includes Desktop, TUI, and Gateway modes with isolated data environments, and bundles tools for offline use, including Python 3.12, PortableGit, and Sysinternals rescue tools.
entries.JackTheGit/hermes-autonomous-server: This project configures Hermes Gateway as a reboot-safe systemd service for headless operation on Ubuntu and Debian servers. It also enables autonomous execution of recurring AI cron jobs and integrates with Nous Portal.
entries.jyje/hermes-agent-helm: This Helm chart deploys Hermes Agent on Kubernetes, with installation available from an OCI registry or a GitHub Pages Helm repository. Optional Copilot and Codex device-login bootstrap and CI testing on an ephemeral kind cluster make it a Kubernetes-focused deployment option.

entries.TauricResearch/TradingAgents: TradingAgents is a financial trading framework that assigns trading tasks to agents in specialized roles and has them discuss strategies dynamically. It is designed for research purposes.
entries.builderz-labs/mission-control: Mission Control is a self-hosted system for governing agent tasks, registrations, memory browsing, and cost tracking. It stands out for offering Web UI, CLI, MCP server, and REST API interfaces, with local Node.js installation or Docker deployment.
entries.agent-of-empires/agent-of-empires: Agent of Empires provides a TUI and web control surface for managing multiple coding agents, including Hermes Agent. It supports persistent tmux sessions, Git worktrees, and multi-repository workspaces, with a web dashboard for structured views, terminal access, and diffs.
entries.shannhk/hermes-agent-control-room: Hermes Agent Control Room is a template for scaling Hermes Agent from a single VPS agent to specialist teams and automated workflows. Its level-based architecture and task bus support delegation and handoffs, and it includes skills for VPS provisioning, security auditing, and backup management.
entries.swarmclawai/swarmclaw: SwarmClaw is a framework for building autonomous agent swarms, with support for 23+ LLM providers, durable agent memory, and MCP tool integration. Visual org charts provide a way to represent team delegation.
entries.agent37-platform/minions: Minions is a control interface for creating, supervising, and reviewing autonomous Hermes Agent work. It combines a Kanban board and live streams of agent reasoning and tool execution with human verification of agent-proposed task completions.
entries.1ilkhamov/opencode-hermes-multiagent: This project coordinates 17 specialized agents across research, planning, implementation, quality, and infrastructure. A strict pipeline architecture and Master Orchestrator handle routing and coordination.
entries.linke-ai/hermes-agent-team: Hermes Agent Team is a local web system for coordinating Leader and Specialist agents through an automated task lifecycle. It integrates MCP and ACP for local tools and communication, with a real-time UI for agent dialogues and Kanban task flows.
entries.howdymary/hermes-agent-metaharness: Hermes Agent Metaharness automates outer-loop optimization of benchmark harness code and orchestrates TBLite and TerminalBench-2 evaluations. It also provides structured candidate mutation and frontier tracking.
entries.runtimenoteslabs/gladiator: Gladiator runs an agent-versus-agent arena in which nine autonomous agents operate across two competing AI companies. Using Paperclip and Hermes Agent for task execution and learning, it displays agent tasks, code, and scoreboard metrics on a real-time dashboard.
entries.InfiniteWhispers/HermesAgent-MultiModel: HermesAgent-MultiModel is a local Mixture-of-Agents framework that queries models in parallel and synthesizes their outputs, using Hermes for task routing and tool-calling. It is designed for consumer GPUs, is optimized for RTX 4080/5080 hardware, and does not require cloud dependencies.

entries.colbymchenry/codegraph: Codegraph builds a local project knowledge graph with `codegraph init` and automatically syncs it as files change. Its MCP server connects that pre-indexed graph to Hermes Agent and other coding agents, with the stated goal of reducing token usage and tool calls.
entries.junhoyeo/tokscale: Tokscale tracks token consumption across multiple AI coding agents, including Hermes, Claude Code, OpenClaw, Codex, and Gemini. It also provides a dashboard for visualizing usage, making it useful for comparing activity across supported clients.
entries.liaohch3/claude-tap: Claude Tap is a local trace viewer for coding-agent API traffic, including traffic from Hermes Agent and several other agents. It lets you inspect prompts, tool calls, streaming responses, and token usage, compare adjacent requests, and redact common auth headers before recording traces.
entries.Javis603/token-monitor: Token Monitor displays real-time token usage, costs, and rate limits for Hermes Agent, Claude Code, Codex, and other supported tools. It also offers historical trends and usage breakdowns, with syncing across multiple devices.
entries.bergside/typeui: TypeUI provides design systems and layout guidance through MCP servers to help build UIs with AI. It works with Hermes Agent and other named assistants, and is compatible with any AI provider that supports markdown or general prompting.
entries.Salomondiei08/oh-my-hermes: Oh My Hermes is an opinionated workflow layer for building, shipping, and operating apps with Hermes Agent, installable with `install.sh`. It includes product-development and operations skills, plus a CTO loop made up of seven focused agents.
entries.joeynyc/hermes-skins: Hermes Skins customizes the Hermes terminal UI with community-made themes, including changes to banner colors, spinners, and ASCII art banners. YAML-based configuration supports theme creation, with examples such as retro DOS and cyberpunk aesthetics.
entries.hermes-labs-ai/lintlang: Lintlang statically checks AI-agent configurations, tool descriptions, system prompts, schemas, and other agent-facing files, using HERM v1.1 scoring. It can report findings as JSON, SARIF, or GitLab Code Quality, and findings are advisory by default unless scans are gated on severity.
entries.tinyhumansai/tiny.place: Tiny.place describes itself as a social economy for autonomous AI agents. It provides encrypted agent-to-agent messaging using Signal Protocol, identity registration with human-readable @handles, and commerce through Solana-based USDC and SOL payments.
entries.unmodeled-tyler/vessel-browser: Vessel Browser is an AI-native browser for autonomous agent control via MCP, with support for Anthropic, OpenAI, Ollama, and other AI providers. Its supervisor sidebar manages agent approvals, checkpoints, and conversation threads, and it supports external MCP clients and browser automation workflows.
entries.AlexAI-MCP/hermes-CCC: Hermes-CCC ports the Hermes Agent brain and 46 core skills to Claude Code Channel, where it runs natively without separate processes or OAuth. It also includes MLOps tools for vLLM, GGUF inference, and RL training.
entries.topoteretes/cognee-integrations: Cognee Integrations is a monorepo of Cognee-owned integration packages organized into two tiers: a permanent knowledge graph and a session cache. Its Claude Code plugin automatically captures and recalls context.
entries.adityahimaone/hermes-agent-rtk-caveman: This setup combines RTK and Caveman templating for CLI workflows, with the project reporting 90–99% token savings. It also includes 40+ preconfigured skills for finance, DevOps, and research, plus automated installation for macOS and Linux.
entries.Abruptive/Ankh.md: Ankh.md is a framework for creating scoped Hermes Agents with per-folder configuration and skills. It supports switching between the default agent and scoped agents, with project-local memories, tools, and custom instructions.
entries.42-evey/evey-setup: evey-setup automates installation of hermes-agent and 12+ supporting services, with three deployment tiers ranging from a minimum viable setup to a production stack. It also supports 29 community plugins across six functional categories.
entries.0xNyk/openclaw-to-hermes: This tool migrates OpenClaw data to Hermes, including SOUL.md, MEMORY.md, skills, and memory archives. It also maps configurations and credentials to Hermes YAML and JSON formats and can set up systemd gateway services.
entries.observeco/observeco: observeco is a Hermes plugin that exports real-time telemetry from agent conversations and monitors multi-agent systems. Its monitoring options include passive analysis and scheduled active probing, while config-aware baselines track performance drift against local file changes.
entries.handnewb/hermes-voice: hermes-voice adds voice interaction to Hermes Agent, with wake-word activation and support for 35 languages via Piper and 9 via Kokoro. It runs offline without API keys or accounts and includes adaptive turn-taking and barge-in.
entries.33hodl/hermes-startup: hermes-startup provides a local runtime that operates with zero network access by default. It requires explicit approval for consequential actions and external writes, and includes contracts for opportunities, offer previews, and exact approvals.
entries.181079342/hermes-memoss: hermes-memoss is a memory plugin that supports semantic search and multi-dimensional memory storage. It provides tools to search, add, and delete memories, with a circuit breaker for MemOS API outages.

entries.farion1231/cc-switch: cc-switch is a cross-platform manager for Hermes Agent and several other agent tools, including Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, OpenClaw, and Gemini CLI. It lets users switch API providers in one click and manage MCP, Skills, and Prompts in one place.
entries.iOfficeAI/AionUi: AionUi is a local open-source cowork app for Hermes Agent and other agent CLIs, with a built-in agent that does not require a separate CLI installation. It includes 21 professional assistants and supports macOS, Windows, and Linux.
entries.nesquena/hermes-webui: hermes-webui provides browser-based access to Hermes Agent, with controls for chats, sessions, and workspaces. It requires no build step, framework, or bundler, and can be accessed through an SSH tunnel.
entries.fathah/hermes-desktop: hermes-desktop is a desktop companion for installing, configuring, and chatting with Hermes Agent, using the official Hermes install script. Its GUI manages profiles, sessions, skills, and tools; the app is available from the project website or GitHub Releases.
entries.EKKOLearnAI/ekko-studio: ekko-studio is a Hermes Agent web dashboard for multi-platform AI chat, session management, scheduled jobs, usage analytics, and channel configuration. It also offers shared and group chats, visual workflows, persistent sessions, and tools for files, voice, devices, and agent management; it is available as a desktop app, npm package, or Docker image.
entries.outsourc-e/hermes-workspace: hermes-workspace brings chat, a terminal, a memory browser, a skills manager, and an inspector into a native web workspace. It also offers Swarm Mode with role-based dispatch and tmux-backed workers, plus a file browser with Monaco and a PTY terminal.
entries.spacering-net/codeg: codeg is a collaborative multi-agent coding workspace that gathers sessions from Hermes, Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, and other agents in a desktop or self-hosted app. Users can import, search, resume, and hand off sessions, delegate across agents, or queue to-dos in worktrees.
entries.dodo-reach/hermes-desktop: This native Mac workspace connects directly to Hermes hosts locally or over SSH, with views for sessions, Kanban, skills, and cron jobs. Its embedded terminal provides direct shell access for system repair.
entries.Eynzof/Hermes-CN-Desktop: Hermes-CN-Desktop is a Windows-first desktop app for Hermes Agent that also supports macOS, with native window and process management. It includes a Hermes-CN-Core kernel with health checks and updates, alongside interfaces for chat, memory management, and LaTeX and Markdown rendering.
entries.abundantbeing/hermes-browser-extension: This Chromium side-panel extension connects the active browser context to a local or remote Hermes Agent runtime, including Hermes Cloud and self-hosted remote connections. Bot Mode supports agent switching and group chats, while Hermes Control is opt-in and Chromium-only.
entries.uzairansaruzi/hermex: hermex is a native SwiftUI iPhone app for driving a self-hosted Hermes agent, pairing with a hermes-webui server. It is a client-only app for iOS 18 and later; users run the server, and the app is free with no analytics or tracking.
entries.freestylefly/wesight: wesight is a desktop AI agent workspace with one-click setup for Hermes Agent, Claude Code, Codex, and OpenClaw, plus custom LLM model routing. Its runtime dashboard tracks token usage and latency, while a live workspace shows code writes and diffs.
entries.joeynyc/hermes-hud: Hermes HUD is an interactive TUI with nine tabs and four selectable color themes for monitoring agent growth, git projects, and scheduled cron jobs. Its tmux operator view also helps manage live agent panes.
entries.jazzyalex/agent-sessions: This native macOS session browser searches prompts, responses, tool activity, errors, and file paths across Hermes agents and other coding-agent CLIs. You can resume supported sessions in Terminal.app, iTerm2, or Warp; session history stays on the Mac, with no telemetry.
entries.xaspx/hermes-control-interface: This self-hosted web dashboard brings a browser-based terminal, file explorer, session overview, cron management, system metrics, and agent status panel into one interface. It also provides real-time chat with tool-call visualization, an MCP server control plane, and a ZOO Swarm Monitor for agent health and kanban pipelines.
entries.nickvasilescu/hermes-desktop-os1: This native macOS workspace runs Hermes Agent on Orgo cloud VMs and SSH hosts, with one-click automated installation on fresh cloud computers. It also includes WebRTC voice mode using OpenAI Realtime and Orgo MCP.
entries.sharbelxyz/hermes-agent-mission-control: This self-hostable mission-control dashboard template connects a local Hermes agent to web dashboards through a Postgres message bus. Its approval inbox lets users review requests with side effects.
entries.liftaris/herm: Herm is an alternative Hermes TUI and dashboard built with OpenTUI for chatting and managing agent sessions. It also combines a kanban board for agentic work with controls for profiles, skills, cron jobs, and toolsets.
entries.clawvader-tech/hermes-telegram-miniapp: This locally run, mobile-first React SPA is a dashboard for Telegram Mini App v2.0, with terminal chat, streaming responses, and file attachments. It supports Telegram validation with dual HMAC-SHA256 and Ed25519 authentication, plus background spawning of up to five concurrent agent instances.
entries.aivrar/portable-hermes-agent: Portable Hermes Agent packages a Windows desktop GUI with 100 tools across more than 20 toolsets, supporting both cloud AI and local models through LM Studio. Its workflow engine supports scheduling, conditions, loops, and parallel execution.
entries.pyrate-llama/hermes-ui: This self-hosted Hermes assistant uses a glassmorphic web interface for chat and real-time log streaming. It pairs an integrated file browser and task-tracking dashboard with tools for managing skills, cron jobs, and MCP servers.
entries.sanchomuzax/hermes-webui: Hermes WebUI is a process-monitoring and configuration dashboard with real-time session activity and cost tracking. It also lets users inspect conversation histories and skill source code, while configuration and environment-variable monitoring is read-only.
entries.Euraika-Labs/pan-ui: Pan-UI is a self-hosted AI workspace centered on chat, with real-time SSE streaming and tool approval cards. Its integrated marketplace offers skills and MCP servers, while isolated profiles keep sessions, memory, and API keys separate.
entries.Felix-Forever/hermes-agent-desktop: This native desktop client supports streaming chat and model switching alongside a PM orchestrator for collaboration among 20 specialized AI agents. It also includes a visual Skill Store with more than 50 curated one-click installations.
entries.robbyczgw-cla/hermes-ui-plus: hermes-ui-plus is an unofficial, open-source interactive chat client for self-hosted Hermes Agent, with answers that can include checklists, choices, forms, and rankings. It also lets you approve or deny commands from your phone and runs on Android, web, macOS, and Linux alpha.
